title: Tiered Court Scene

inscriptions.inscription: [[verso, in Persian]] bi-mowjib arza-dasht fadawi bi-hokm-i qadr-i tu'am huzur lami al-nur-i jinab-i aqdas Chitarman-i musawwar amal nimud
inscriptions.inscription_translation: According to the lowly instructions of your devoted servant following the verbal commands [lit.: command twinned with presence] of the luminous most sacred [aqdas, referring to the emperor], Chitarman the painter carried out the task [i.e., painted, amal nimud].
inscriptions.inscription_remark: The word aqdas is placed well above the rest of the inscription on the top left as a measure of honor in the traditional way of spacing the handwriting to convey utmost respect, as found in Mughal and Safavid official documents.

inscriptions.inscription_translation: The seal refers to "the devoted servant [of the house of] Muhammad Shah, Padshah-i Ghazi."

did_you_know: A leering sea horse monster rears its head below the golden island city of Lanka.
description: Emperor Muhammad Shah rekindled an imperial interest in Hinduism that had not been so strong since the time of Akbar, 150 years before. He commissioned this painting that shows the acts of Rama, hero of a Hindu epic, who slays the demon of the golden city of Lanka at the top of the page. In the middle sections, various Hindu deities enjoy music, kite flying, and boating, while at the bottom the Krishna plays Holi with his lover Radha and other palace women. They shoot red-colored water at one another with plunger guns in celebration of the coming of spring.
